variants.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Create one refined Freelancer RH PIRATE / JUNKER FREIGHTER concept sheet, with three coherent views. The user rejects the previous boxy roof design. REBUILD THE DORSAL HUMP FROM THE ACTUAL ORIGINAL MODEL. This is the highest priority alongside the immutable original cabin.

REFERENCE ROLES:
Image 1 is the actual installed freighter: authoritative original dimensions, characteristic tall ROUND ARCHED HUMP, deep rectangular cargo body, exact cockpit size/location and compact aft engines.
Image 2 is an offline sequence of its ACTUAL cargo mechanism: CLOSED, OPENING and OPEN. The two solid semicircular side CHEEKS remain FIXED; the broad curved shutter BETWEEN THEM rotates aft and DOWN into the rear of the body about a transverse horizontal axis, around 120 degrees. This is not a box roof, a turret, an upward-hinged lid or an exterior skeleton. Learn the real geometry; do not copy the six-view reference layout.
Image 3 is the immutable original freighter cockpit: preserve this precise module, shape, size, pane divisions, sloping upper blue windshield, opaque pale lower wall with separated rectangular blue slots, thin yellow-black edges, chin and small underside equipment box. No redesigned cabin and no continuous lower blue visor.
Image 4 is the executed RH pirate elite for inset-panel craftsmanship and worn pirate material vocabulary ONLY. Do not import its overall architecture or cabin.
Image 5 is the latest M09 concept for DETAIL DENSITY ONLY. Its roof form is WRONG and must NOT be copied. Add approximately FIFTY PERCENT more purposeful medium-size detail than M09, while preserving calm readable planes. Aim between sparse M and crowded older D.

ESSENTIAL ROTATING ROOF FORM:
The dorsal outline in SIDE is a HIGH NEAR-SEMICIRCULAR ARC, like the upper segment of a large transverse drum rising above the shoulder. Match the source hump's height, radius, longitudinal extent and narrow transverse width. Use about 10-12 broad authored facets to describe this ROUND ARC, retaining the rising and falling curvature all the way across the crown. No flat truncated pyramid, trapezoidal roof box, low wedge, tiny roof cap or elongated warehouse ridge.
The broad outer shutter spans BETWEEN the two closed arc-shaped sidewalls, with 6-8 broad transverse pressed panel sectors following the circular surface. These are continuous solid sheet-metal shutter panels, not separate bars, ribs or open roller slats. Allow shallow recessed transverse panel fields, purposeful red replacement sectors and a few offset service covers, all inside the shutter's cylindrical sweep envelope. Clearly readable thin motion seams along its two curved side margins. Two fixed thick solid side cheeks have recessed concentric arc fields and 4-6 broad radial inset sectors, not spoked wheels or external hoop frames. These circular features explain the hinge radius. Do not bridge the moving shutter to fixed hull with a plate, vent, pipe or brace. In this sheet all THREE views show the shutter CLOSED; its mechanism must be believable from its curved shell and clear separation. Preserve the future native rearward/downward rotation and free swept path.

HULL AND DETAIL:
Native flight size width 9.465, height 11.463, length 23.722 units: tall narrow freighter, not a fat transport or tiny fighter. The original cabin remains unchanged and full sized. The LOWER hull is angular: strong sharp cargo-volume cuts, stepped joined donor housings, deep closed-backed cargo-door recess, varied shoulder planes and a meaningful lower sill. Source circular roof and angular hull must work together.
About 50% more medium-size detail than image 5: on each side one large recessed cargo hatch with a designed stepped jamb and two unequal inset fields, two or three smaller service panels at useful locations, a deep ventilation pocket with 3-4 broad blades, a few substantial housing joints and shaped engine roots. Original cylinder sleeves receive one robust collar and a recessed closed endcap. No evenly repeated tiny boxes, numerous fasteners, busy lines over every plane or indiscriminate grunge. Use the elite's carefully seated red inset fields, closed returns and clear plane changes.
Exactly THREE short retractable closed-ended cylinders per SIDE, one larger central and two smaller fore/aft, ONE row, six total. Thick solid integral side cheeks, no wings. All are extended for FLIGHT and must withdraw laterally into the side housings at base. Keep original mechanisms and symmetrical positions. Exactly TWO aft engines at same height, one overlapping silhouette in SIDE and two visible in TOP, original-sized modules on short solid closed couplers. Keep a readable rear housing/exhaust arrangement reminiscent of the original. No weapons attached.
Scavenger character comes from genuine rebuilt donor volumes, physically different fitted sections, deep red reclaimed panels, restrained asymmetry of fixed covers and repaired major joints. Retain Freelancer Rheinland heritage.
No exposed pipes, hoses, cables, external trusses, skeletal frames, braces, cages, separate external ribs, wings or claws. The solid arched side cheeks are necessary bodywork, not an open external frame. No modeled rivet fields. Do not round every angular hull corner. Circular curvature is REQUIRED for the actual rotating roof, not a general smoothing treatment.

PAGE:
Landscape off-white concept paper, confident ink outlines with controlled gouache/marker shading, clear medium-size relief. Pale worn metal, muted donor red and sparse faded olive, dark recesses; controlled weathering without visual noise. Large front-side 3/4 LEFT, true SIDE / FLIGHT upper RIGHT (nose right), true TOP / FLIGHT lower RIGHT (nose up). Exactly three complete uncropped views of the SAME ship, consistent semicircular roof, hatch geometry, original cockpit, 3 cylinders each side and two engines. No additional inset or detached part. Only title and SIDE / FLIGHT, TOP / FLIGHT labels.

VARIANT P01: Closest-to-source dimensional hierarchy. Preserve the original proudly round hump and deep cargo block, but redesign the body with chamfered vertical fore/aft corners, two stepped closed drum-carrier housings and a recessed lower hatch offset toward the aft half. A wide fixed red arcuate field in each side cheek carries a few broad radial recesses. The curved shutter has eight broad crosswise pressed sectors; two are salvaged muted red, the rest pale. Add a well-shaped deep service pocket behind the cabin, a recessed side vent and compact stepped engine collars. The source hump remains clearly circular and mechanically separate, not swallowed by the shoulder. Title exactly: RH JUNKER FREIGHTER / P01
